notes: McElreath, Statistical Rethinking 2nd ed. ch 13: varying intercepts on actor (7 chimps) and block (6). The 4-level treatment index is prosoc_left x condition. recipient (mostly NA), chose_prosoc (alternate outcome) and trial ignored.

McElreath ch 11/13: Berkeley graduate admissions, admit out of applications per dept x gender (12 rows). ch 11 fits dept as a fixed index; the varying-intercept (1 | dept) version is the multilevel reading the caller flagged. reject = applications - admit.
McElreath ch 13/14: contraceptive use of 1934 women in 60 districts, varying intercept and urban slope by district. woman is the row id.

formula: response ~ action + intention + contact + action:intention + contact:intention + (1 | id) + (1 | story)
notes: McElreath ch 12: ordered-logit of moral-permissibility ratings (1-7). ch 12 fits it as a fixed ordered logit with the action:intention and contact:intention interactions; the varying intercepts on id (person) and story are the ch 12 multilevel extension. edu (ordered), age, male, order, case, action2 ignored.

Oxford boys growth: repeated heights of 26 boys over 9 standardised ages; varying intercept and slope on age per Subject (the caller's multilevel example). Occasion is the within-boy index, redundant with age.

McElreath growth example: body mass over age for 6 dinosaur species. The book fits species-specific nonlinear growth curves (not a mixed model); species repeats within the table so it is the grouping factor per the #24 rule, rendered as a random intercept and age slope at low confidence. sp_id duplicates species.

formula: NoDisperse ~ Species + Male + Mother + Sisters + Bros + ClanSize + AllKin + (1 | Year)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: NoDisperse (did not disperse, 0/1) is the natal-dispersal outcome the study measures against kin presence (Mother, Sisters, Bros, ClanSize, AllKin). Grouped by Year (cohort, 1976-; definitely repeated); Species is kept as a covariate because its level count could not be verified from the help page, Species as a second grouping factor is the alternative. No Rd in the package.

formula: cbind(num_amtl, sockets - num_amtl) ~ age + tooth_class + prob_male + (1 | specimen)
notes: Ante-mortem tooth loss: num_amtl teeth lost out of sockets for each specimen x tooth_class (Anterior/Posterior/Premolar), ~483 specimens with 3 rows each. Binomial with a random intercept per specimen, age/tooth_class/prob_male covariates. No model in the package help; grouping inferred. stdev_age, genus, pop ignored.

RESPONSE INFERRED: kg.meat (meat returned) is the foraging-return outcome by hunter age over many hunting days; id = hunter (repeated), the grouping factor. hours (time hunting) a covariate/effort; date columns and datatype ignored. No Rd.

Social-learning box-choice experiment: y is the chosen option (1/2/3) for children across several cultures; culture is the grouping factor (children nested in cultures). No model in the help; grouping and response inferred from column names.

Primate between-group contest outcomes: win (focal wins, 0/1) with crossed random intercepts on focal and other (the two contestants). dyad and the group-composition counts (n/m/f) ignored; dyad is largely one row per level. No Rd; grouping inferred.
RESPONSE INFERRED: pages (dissertation length) by field; major is the grouping factor (many dissertations per field), year a covariate. No Rd.

Sampson monastery social network: like_AB is the directed liking count from monk A to B, with crossed sender (A) and receiver (B) random intercepts. like_BA, dislike_AB, dislike_BA are the other directed outcomes; dyad_id is one row per dyad; names ignored. No Rd; social-relations grouping inferred.

Seshat moralizing-gods data: presence of moralizing gods (0/1, many years unknown/NaN) by polity over time; polity is the grouping factor (panel over years). population and writing covariates. Rows without a measured response dropped by the merge. No Rd.

McElreath ch 11 practice: Dutch NWO grant awards out of applications per discipline x gender (18 rows). ch 11 fits discipline as a fixed index (confound example); the varying-intercept (1 | discipline) version is the natural multilevel reading.

formula: nuts_opened ~ age + sex + hammer + offset(log(seconds)) + (1 | chimpanzee)
notes: McElreath ch 16: nut-opening counts per bout with duration seconds (offset). The book fits a theoretical nonlinear strength-growth Poisson model (strength rises with age), without a chimpanzee random effect; chimpanzee repeats within the table so it is the grouping factor per the #24 rule, rendered here as a plain count GLMM at low confidence. help ignored.

formula: social_learning ~ research_effort + brain + body + group_size + (1 | genus)
notes: McElreath ch 14 phylogenetic regression: counts of observed social learning across 301 primate species. The book's model is a Gaussian process over the species phylogeny (observation-level), not a genus random effect; genus repeats within the table (species share genera) so it is the grouping factor per the #24 rule, at low confidence. Life-history columns and ids ignored.

von Bortkiewicz Prussian horse-kick deaths: kicks per corps per year (14 corps x 20 years), a count panel. A variance-components model with crossed corps and year random intercepts; no covariates. No Rd.
Rinderpest mortality out of n cattle per herd x stock (large/small), 11 herds x 2 rows. Binomial with a random intercept per herd and a stock covariate. No model in the help; grouping inferred.

UFC fight outcomes and left-handedness: fighter1.win (0/1) with crossed random intercepts on the two fighters (each appears in several fights) and lefty-indicator covariates. fight/episode ids ignored. No Rd; grouping inferred.

formula: score ~ wine.amer + judge.amer + flight + (1 | judge) + (1 | wine)
notes: McElreath practice: 2012 wine-judging scores, crossed varying intercepts on judge (9) and wine (20) with American-origin indicators and flight (white/red) as covariates.

Urban fox body weights (Rd: group, avgfood, groupsize, area, weight). McElreath ch 5-6 uses it as a DAG/backdoor example with fixed effects; group (fox social group, 30 groups of 2-8) repeats and is the grouping factor per the #24 rule, at low confidence.

Primate milk composition (Rd, Hinde & Milligan 2011): milk energy density by neocortex percent and maternal mass. McElreath ch 5-6 fits it without random effects; clade (4 taxonomic groups, several species each) repeats and is the grouping factor per the #24 rule. perc.fat/protein/lactose are alternate composition responses.

McElreath ch 8 interaction example: tulip blooms by water and shade. The book fits blooms ~ water * shade with fixed effects; bed (3 greenhouse beds a/b/c, 9 plants each) repeats and is the grouping factor per the #24 rule, at low confidence.

formula: giftsAB ~ dlndist + dass + offset(offset) + (1 | hidA) + (1 | hidB)
notes: McElreath ch 14 social-relations (gift-exchange) model: directed gift counts giftsAB between 25 households, crossed giver (hidA) and receiver (hidB) random intercepts, log-distance (dlndist) and association (dass) covariates, offset. giftsBA is the reverse-direction response and did (one row per dyad) carries the correlated dyad effect in the full model; drel1-4 are the relationship-type dummies.

WWG ch 3: rat-pup birth weights, random intercept per litter, treatment (High/Low/Control) x sex interaction and litter size. The final model also fits heterogeneous residual variance by treatment group, not representable in lme4. pup.id is the row id.

formula: mathgain ~ mathkind + sex + minority + ses + yearstea + mathknow + mathprep + housepov + (1 | schoolid) + (1 | schoolid:classid)
notes: WWG ch 4: three-level model of first-grade math gain, random intercepts for school and classroom-within-school, with student-, classroom- and school-level covariates. classid nested in schoolid (merge builds the composite). childid is the student id.

WWG ch 5: nucleotide activation in 5 rats measured across 2 treatments x 3 brain regions (30 rows), random intercept per animal with a treatment-by-region interaction. The Rd's examples wrap treatment and region in factor().

formula: gcf ~ time + base.gcf + cda + age + (time | patient) + (1 | patient:tooth)
notes: WWG ch 7: dental-veneer gingival crevicular fluid, three levels (tooth nested in patient), random intercept and time slope at the patient level and a random intercept per tooth. base.gcf, cda and age are tooth/patient-level covariates. Matches the Stata [ME] veneer reading.

WWG ch 6: longitudinal socialization (VSAE) of 214 autistic children at ages 2-13, random intercept and growth slope per child, with baseline expressive-language group (sicdegp, 3-level factor) and its interaction with age. The book fits a quadratic (age and age-squared) growth; polynomial terms are not representable, so age is named once (d_doc counts the linear term).

formula: CD4 ~ time + age + smoke + drug + partners + cesd + (time | id)
notes: Diggle, Heagerty, Liang & Zeger ch 1/5: CD4 counts of HIV seroconverters over time since seroconversion, random intercept and time slope per subject (id). CD4 is an integer count column modelled as a Gaussian LMM (often sqrt-transformed), so filed continuous rather than count. Covariates from the banner: age, smoking, drug use, partners, CESD depression score.
